title: The Intertwined Legacies of Gloria Steinem and Dolly Parton

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·荣森，欢迎收看《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周围文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 甚至在黑胶唱片时代的夜总会当DJ的时候，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每天晚上都要带上300件你最珍爱的藏品去工作，把DJ台变成这样一个充满活力的、由美丽且有50年历史的艺术品组成的快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你喜爱的播客平台上收听爱彼推出的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Hi, this is Rachel Abrams from the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是《纽约时报》的雷切尔·阿布拉姆斯。

sentences.en: Hi, Rachel.
sentences.zh: 嗨，雷切尔。

sentences.en: Thank you for making time to speak with us.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你抽空与我们交谈。

sentences.en: I'm sorry for your loss.
sentences.zh: 对于你的损失，我感到很遗憾。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Big one.
sentences.zh: 一个巨大的人。

sentences.en: Big, big one.
sentences.zh: 一个非常、非常巨大的人。

sentences.en: On Thursday morning, hours after the death of the feminist icon Gloria Steinem, we reached out to one of her longtime friends and colleagues,
sentences.zh: 周四上午，在女权主义偶像格洛丽亚·斯泰纳姆去世几小时后，我们联系了她的一位老朋友兼同事，

sentences.en: Letty Cotton Pogrebin.
sentences.zh: 莱蒂·科顿·波格雷宾。

sentences.en: How did you first hear about the news of Gloria's passing?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么第一次听到格洛丽亚去世的消息的？

sentences.en: Robin called me at 6.44 a.m.
sentences.zh: 罗宾在早上6点44分给我打电话，

sentences.en: and I was scared to take the call.
sentences.zh: 而我当时很害怕接听这个电话。

sentences.en: And then it was Gloria.
sentences.zh: 然后电话那头是格洛丽亚。

sentences.en: And, you know, I thought it might be, God forbid, someone in my family.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我当时以为，天哪，千万别是我家里的什么人。

sentences.en: Then I realized she was my family.
sentences.zh: 然后我意识到她就是我的家人。

sentences.en: She was your family.
sentences.zh: 她就像你的家人一样。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: She was.
sentences.zh: 她是。

sentences.en: Gloria has been in my life for 55 years.
sentences.zh: 格洛丽亚在我的生命中存在了55年。

sentences.en: So I met her in 1971 at the founding conference of the National Women's Political Caucus.
sentences.zh: 所以我是在1971年全国女性政治核心小组的成立大会上结识她的。

sentences.en: And we ended up talking until three in the morning.
sentences.zh: 我们最后一直聊到了凌晨三点。

sentences.en: She was interested in everyone.
sentences.zh: 她对每个人都感兴趣。

sentences.en: She thought every woman's life was a novel, a story.
sentences.zh: 她认为每个女性的生活都是一部小说、一个故事。

sentences.en: You know, she saw women's lives in all the complexity of women's lives.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，她看到了女性生活中所有的复杂性。

sentences.en: She didn't see us as any one thing.
sentences.zh: 她没有把我们看作是单一的某种东西。

sentences.en: And she knew somewhere in every woman there was tragedy, comedy, and meaning.
sentences.zh: 而且她知道，在每个女性的内心深处，都存在着悲剧、喜剧和意义。

sentences.en: Word of Steinem's death came as many Americans were still grieving the loss of another iconic woman, Dolly Parton.
sentences.zh: 在斯泰纳姆逝世的消息传出时，许多美国人仍在为失去另一位标志性女性多莉·帕顿而悲痛。

sentences.en: Dolly Parton passed away.
sentences.zh: 多莉·帕顿去世了。

sentences.en: She's such an exceptional singer.
sentences.zh: 她是一位如此杰出的歌手。

sentences.en: Beautiful voice.
sentences.zh: 有着美妙的嗓音。

sentences.en: To me, she was kind of like a guiding light.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，她有点像指路明灯。

sentences.en: She's kind of like our matriarch, our country's queen, in a sense.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，她有点像我们的女族长，我们国家的女王。

sentences.en: And she just has always been good and just embodies good, reflects good back to people.
sentences.zh: 她一直以来都是善良的，并且化身为善良本身，将善良回馈给人们。

sentences.en: And I think that that's so important.
sentences.zh: 我认为这非常重要。

sentences.en: On paper, the connections between these two women seem faint and superficial.
sentences.zh: 从纸面上看，这两位女性之间的联系似乎微弱而肤浅。

sentences.en: But for my colleague, Times Magazine writer Susan Dominus, the relationship between their lives and their impact was inescapable.
sentences.zh: 但对于我的同事、《时报杂志》撰稿人苏·多米努斯来说，她们生活与影响之间的关系是不可避免的。

sentences.en: It's Friday, September 4th.
sentences.zh: 今天是9月4日，星期五。

sentences.en: Hey, Sue.
sentences.zh: 嘿，苏。

sentences.en: Hi, Michael.
sentences.zh: 嗨，迈克尔。

sentences.en: I think it's fair to say it's been a tough week and a half.
sentences.zh: 我认为可以坦率地说，过去的一个半星期非常艰难。

sentences.en: I think it's fair to say it's been pretty emotional for a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 我认为可以公平地说，对许多人来说，这段时间相当情绪化。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, tell me how you have been thinking about these back-to-back deaths of these two hugely important women, Dolly Parton and Gloria Steinem.
sentences.zh: 好吧，告诉我你是如何看待这两位极其重要的女性——多莉·帕顿和格洛丽亚·斯泰纳姆相继离世的？

sentences.en: Well, to start, I have to say that the timing of their deaths so close together has really been, I think,
sentences.zh: 首先，我必须说，她们去世的时间如此接近，这真的让我思考，

sentences.en: something that's made me reflect on the way they were influential almost as a duo in my life and for probably a lot of other women around my age or maybe a little bit older or a little bit younger.
sentences.zh: 她们在我的生命中几乎就像是以二人组的形式产生着影响，对于和我差不多年纪、或者可能稍大一点、又或者稍小一点的许多其他女性来说，大概也是如此。

sentences.en: But, you know, I came of age in the 70s, and in a way, I almost can't remember a time when I didn't know who Gloria Steinem was.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，我在70年代迎来青春期，在某种程度上，我甚至记不起自己不知道格洛丽亚·斯泰纳姆是谁的时光。

sentences.en: You know, she represented feminism with a capital F, and she was fighting for a world in which women could fully express themselves and be their most powerful selves,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，她代表了带有大写F的女权主义，她为一个女性能够充分表达自我、展现最具力量的自我的世界而战，

sentences.en: but was also advocating for the world to change, too.
sentences.zh: 但她同时也主张世界也应该随之改变。

sentences.en: She was fighting for structural change, for political change, for legal change.
sentences.zh: 她为结构性变革、政治变革、法律变革而战。

sentences.en: And in a lot of cases, achieving it.
sentences.zh: 而且在很多情况下，她都实现了这些。

sentences.en: Yeah, and that is definitely, I think, the side of feminism that we deflect to most often when we think about it.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这绝对是我们想到女权主义时最常倾向的那一面。

sentences.en: But the other side of feminism is the women who weren't claiming that label of feminism,
sentences.zh: 但女权主义的另一面是那些没有声称自己带有女权主义标签的女性，

sentences.en: but were nonetheless out there and acting and living the promise of what feminism was trying to offer to women, which is to say financial independence, total control of your life,
sentences.zh: 但她们依然走出去，付诸行动，并活出了女权主义试图赋予女性的承诺，也就是经济独立、对生活的完全掌控，

sentences.en: an unapologetic inhabiting of who it was that you wanted to be,
sentences.zh: 毫无歉意地活出你想成为的那个自己，

sentences.en: and insisting on that kind of woman's right to be strong and to be fearless, and that was Dolly Parton, who, by the way,
sentences.zh: 并坚持女性拥有这种变得坚强、无所畏惧的权利，那就是多莉·帕顿，顺便说一句，

sentences.en: often danced around the word feminism and even often tried to avoid it.
sentences.zh: 她经常绕开“女权主义”这个词，甚至经常试图避开它。

sentences.en: And frankly, I don't think she's necessarily the first person people think of when they think of feminism.
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，当人们想到女权主义时，我认为她不一定是大家首先想到的人。

sentences.en: But the fact of their dying so close to each other has really made me realize that feminism needed both of those representations of what women could do.
sentences.zh: 但她们相继离世的事实确实让我意识到，女权主义需要女性能够做到这一点的这两种表征。

sentences.en: It needed the person who was the explicit organizer and the rallier and the articulator of what these specific values were.
sentences.zh: 它需要那个明确的组织者、动员者以及这些具体价值观阐述者的人。

sentences.en: But it also needed that person who was just embodying it and embodying it with so much joy and so much power.
sentences.zh: 但它也需要那个仅仅是将其实践出来、并且带着如此多的喜悦与力量将其付诸实践的人。

sentences.en: Well, talk, Sue, about the two very different lives and two very different approaches of these women and how you yourself experience them in your own life.
sentences.zh: 那么，苏，来谈谈这两位女性截然不同的人生和截然不同的方法，以及你自己如何在生活中体验到她们的。

sentences.en: And because she died just within the past 24 hours or so, let's start with Gloria Steinem and how she comes into your consciousness.
sentences.zh: 鉴于她是在过去24小时左右内去世的，让我们从格洛丽亚·斯泰纳姆开始，谈谈她是如何进入你的意识的。

sentences.en: So I've only recently thought a little bit about the fact that I was born on September 1st, 1970,
sentences.zh: 所以我最近才开始思考这样一个事实：我出生于1970年9月1日，

sentences.en: which was just a few days after one of these big inflection points in the feminist movement when there was this huge women's strike and 50,000 women marched on Fifth Avenue and closed it down.
sentences.zh: 那正是在女权主义运动的重大转折点之一的几天后，当时举行了一场盛大的女性罢工，5万名女性在第五大道游行并将其封锁。

sentences.en: Well, the main demand, of course, is equal rights, equal rights to have a job, to have respect, to not be viewed as a piece of meat.
sentences.zh: 好吧，主要的诉求当然是权利平等，拥有工作的平等权利，获得尊重的平等权利，不被视为一块肉的平等权利。

sentences.en: And I grew up with the rise of feminism, which is to say the omnipresence of Gloria Steinem.
sentences.zh: 我是伴随着女权主义的崛起而长大的，也就是格洛丽亚·斯泰纳姆的无处不在。

sentences.en: I would not have admitted my own inequality, even though I had been refused apartments by landlords who would not rent to women.
sentences.zh: 我不会承认自身的不平等，尽管我曾被拒绝向女性出租房屋的房东拒绝过。

sentences.en: She was everywhere.
sentences.zh: 她无处不在。

sentences.en: I no longer accept society's judgment that my group is second class.
sentences.zh: 我不再接受社会对我的群体属于二等公民的判断。

sentences.en: And she was somebody who I remember kind of in the background of my entire experience of growing up in the 70s as a kid in a household with tons of magazines lying around.
sentences.zh: 在我70年代作为孩子在家里到处都是杂志的家庭中成长的整个经历中，我记得她有点像是背景般的存在。

sentences.en: And what exactly was she saying?
sentences.zh: 她究竟在说些什么？

sentences.en: And in particular, what was she saying about feminism and women?
sentences.zh: 特别是，她对女权主义和女性说了些什么？

sentences.en: So she really entered feminism through journalism.
sentences.zh: 所以她实际上是通过新闻业进入女权主义领域的。

sentences.en: Her big first breakout piece of journalism was famously,
sentences.zh: 她第一篇名声大噪的新闻大作是众所周知的，

sentences.en: she went undercover as a playboy bunny and revealed that this job that people from the outside thought was maybe kind of glamorous and fun was actually grueling.
sentences.zh: 她隐瞒身份潜入花花公子俱乐部，并揭露了这份在局外人看来或许有点光鲜亮丽且有趣的工作实际上极其折磨人。

sentences.en: It was humiliating.
sentences.zh: 这是极其羞辱人的。

sentences.en: The women there were exposed to all kinds of harassment.
sentences.zh: 那里的女性暴露在各种骚扰之下。

sentences.en: They were required to take these invasive gynecological exaMs.
sentences.zh: 她们被要求接受这些具有侵入性的妇科检查。

sentences.en: You know, they were underpaid.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，她们的薪水过低。

sentences.en: They worked long hours.
sentences.zh: 她们长时间工作。

sentences.en: And it was a piece of stunt journalism in a way, but then it got her a lot of attention.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，这是一篇噱头新闻，但它随后为她赢得了极大的关注。

sentences.en: But she didn't really become active as a feminist per se until the late 60s when she was reporting on a group of women who were openly discussing their abortions.
sentences.zh: 但直到60年代末，当她报道一群公开讨论她们堕胎经历的女性时，她才真正作为严格意义上的女权主义者活跃起来。

sentences.en: And she ended up writing a piece for New York Magazine about the women's liberation movement.
sentences.zh: 她最终为《纽约》杂志撰写了一篇关于妇女解放运动的文章。

sentences.en: From there, I think public speaking invitations started flowing in.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，我认为公众演讲的邀请开始纷至沓来。

sentences.en: And all of this ultimately leads to her co-founding what became Ms. Magazine, which was an incredible manifesto for women of the time and was immediately a huge hit.
sentences.zh: 所有这一切最终促成了她共同创立了后来的《女士》杂志，这对当时的女性来说是一份不可思议的宣言，并且一经推出就获得了巨大成功。

sentences.en: It started because there were just a great many women writers and editors who didn't feel that they were working on magazines that they read and that they had the opportunity to really be honest about their own experiences in a magazine.
sentences.zh: 它的创立是因为有大量女性作家和编辑觉得她们工作的不是她们自己阅读的杂志，也没有机会在杂志上真正诚实地表达她们自己的经历。

sentences.en: It was the first magazine run entirely by women.
sentences.zh: 这是第一本完全由女性运营的杂志。

sentences.en: And unlike other women's magazines, it was leaning into controversial subjects.
sentences.zh: 与其他女性杂志不同，它倾向于涉及有争议的主题。

sentences.en: You know, how to get equal pay, legally speaking, or extra legally, how to take the license away from the television station that's discriminating against women,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如何在法律意义上或法律之外获得同工同酬，如何剥夺歧视女性的电视台的执照，

sentences.en: how to start a child care center, how to get into medical school.
sentences.zh: 如何创办托儿所，如何进入医学院学习。

sentences.en: You know, it's very strong on how-to articles with the simple assumption that this is possible.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，它非常注重实用文章，其简单的假设就是这一切都是可能的。

sentences.en: It also, I think, really encouraged other women's magazines ultimately to cover those topics too.
sentences.zh: 我认为它最终也确实极大地鼓励了其他女性杂志去报道这些话题。

sentences.en: So it was a juggernaut that changed the face of pop cultural media consumption for women.
sentences.zh: 因此，它是一个改变了女性流行文化媒体消费面貌的庞然大物。

sentences.en: Eventually, of course, though, she leaps from journalism into this much more formal advocacy and organizing and into politics.
sentences.zh: 当然，最终她还是从新闻界跨界到了这种更正式的倡导、组织以及政治领域。

sentences.en: Very quickly, yeah.
sentences.zh: 非常快，是的。

sentences.en: I mean, obviously she was really an important messenger through the media, but she was also an organizer.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，显然她通过媒体真正成为了一个重要的信使，但她同时也是一个组织者。

sentences.en: We are the women that our parents warned us about.
sentences.zh: 我们就是我们父母警告我们要防范的女性。

sentences.en: We have got here a revolution.
sentences.zh: 我们在这里迎来了一场革命。

sentences.en: She was fighting for the ERA.
sentences.zh: 她在为《平等权利修正案》而战。

sentences.en: Stand here not only for the Equal Rights Amendment, but in the names of all the women in this country who struggle with two jobs when men have won.
sentences.zh: 今天站在这里，不仅是为了《平等权利修正案》，也是为了这个国家所有那些在男性已经获胜的情况下还要做两份工作的女性。

sentences.en: She was helping to found the National Women's Political Caucus.
sentences.zh: 她协助创立了全国女性政治核心小组。

sentences.en: She was very active in union organizing.
sentences.zh: 她在工会组织活动中非常活跃。

sentences.en: This inhuman system of exploitation will change, but only if we force it to change.
sentences.zh: 这种惨无人道的剥削制度将会改变，但前提是我们强迫它改变。

sentences.en: And she was basically someone who stood for equality in the workplace, women's control of their reproductive rights, an end to all kinds of double standards,
sentences.zh: 她基本上是一个支持职场平等、女性控制自身生育权利、结束各种双重标准的人，

sentences.en: and a real shift in what home life ideally would look like.
sentences.zh: 并且真正改变了理想中家庭生活的模样。

sentences.en: Well, as Steinem and those around her are coming at this question of women's equality and liberation from all these different angles,
sentences.zh: 那么，当斯泰纳姆及其周围的人从所有这些不同的角度来探讨女性平等与解放的问题时，

sentences.en: what were you and those around you making of the message?
sentences.zh: 你和你周围的人对这些信息作何感想？

sentences.en: If I'm really honest, I think in some ways it was an uncomfortable time for many people, maybe even including a little suburban kid.
sentences.zh: 如果我足够诚实的话，我认为在某些方面，对许多人来说这是一个令人感到不适的时代，甚至可能包括一个小小的郊区小孩。

sentences.en: You know, I think feminism in general, the feminism I associated with Steinem, had this image that was a little bit harsh, maybe.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我认为总的来说，我与斯泰纳姆联系在一起的女权主义，给人的形象有点刺耳，也许吧。

sentences.en: You know, the songs, even if you think about the anthems, it was like, I am woman, hear me roar.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，那些歌曲，即使你想想那些口号，就像是，我是女性，听我怒吼。

sentences.en: Or, you know, or it was Aretha Franklin, God bless her, demanding respect.
sentences.zh: 或者，你知道的，或者那是艾瑞莎·弗兰克林，愿上帝保佑她，在要求得到尊重。

sentences.en: Or it was later, like, I will survive.
sentences.zh: 或者后来像，我会活下去。

sentences.en: All these things that are really important, but were a little bit maybe intimidating for a kid.
sentences.zh: 所有这些事情都非常重要，但对一个孩子来说可能有点令人生畏。

sentences.en: And I kind of associated feminism maybe because of more conservative messages that were also being filtered through.
sentences.zh: 我把女权主义联系在一起，也许是因为那些同样被过滤进来的更保守的信息。

sentences.en: I associated it with why that mom around the corner, you know, walked out on her family.
sentences.zh: 我把它与街角那个抛弃家庭的妈妈联系在一起。

sentences.en: Or I associated it with why my favorite summer camp counselor made fun of me for reading Seventeen magazine because it was all about how to look cute for boys or, you know,
sentences.zh: 或者我把它与我最喜欢的夏令营辅导员因为我读《十七岁》杂志而嘲笑我联系在一起，因为那本杂志讲的全是如何为男孩打扮得可爱，或者是，

sentences.en: how to sew things from leftover dish rags.
sentences.zh: 如何用剩下的洗碗布缝制东西。

sentences.en: Like women aren't supposed to be patting themselves on the back or drawing attention to themselves and their glory.
sentences.zh: 就像女性不应该自我标榜或把注意力吸引到自己和荣誉上一样。

sentences.en: Of course, she was doing that to bring business and job opportunities to the community in which she was raised.
sentences.zh: 当然，她这样做是为了给自己的家乡社区带来商业和就业机会。

sentences.en: That was the motivation.
sentences.zh: 这才是她的动机。

sentences.en: It wasn't about self-glorification.
sentences.zh: 这并不是为了自我标榜。

sentences.en: But I think it was a modeling of power that is very, very rare in female business history.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得这树立了一种权力的典范，这在女性商业史上极其罕见。

sentences.en: And she was a tremendous businesswoman who really kept control and fought for control of her own creative output in a way that no doubt paved the way for people like Taylor Swift,
sentences.zh: 她是一位了不起的女商人，真正保持了对自己创作成果的控制权并为此抗争，毫无疑问，这为像泰勒·斯威夫特这样的人铺平了道路，

sentences.en: who, you know, have inspired so many young women with her fierceness and the way that she conducts herself as a businesswoman.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，泰勒以她的坚韧以及作为女商人的行事方式，激励了无数年轻女性。

sentences.en: So what you came to understand is that the woman who played that character in 9 to 5, battling a chauvinist boss and a toxic male culture,
sentences.zh: 所以你逐渐明白，那个在《朝九晚五》中饰演与沙文主义老板和有毒男性文化抗争的女性，

sentences.en: was a woman who through song and through her business modeled what a woman could be in practice.
sentences.zh: 其实是一位通过歌声和商业实践，为女性应有面貌树立典范的女性。

sentences.en: And what that could be was a bonafide business mogul.
sentences.zh: 而那样的面貌，正是一位货真价实的商业大亨。

sentences.en: Yeah, think about it.
sentences.zh: 是的，想想看。

sentences.en: In many ways, she was executing the vision of what feminists wanted women to be able to do.
sentences.zh: 在许多方面，她正在将女性主义者希望女性能够做到的愿景付诸实践。

sentences.en: And on behalf of myself and the Internal Revenue Service, I'd like to thank Whitney for making my song such an enormous hit.
sentences.zh: 我谨代表我自己和美国国家税务局，感谢惠特尼把我的歌变得如此大红大紫。

sentences.en: She had control over her finances and over her business.
sentences.zh: 她掌握着自己的财务和商业主权。

sentences.en: You know, I look like a woman, but I think like a man.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我看起来像个女人，但我的思维像个男人。

sentences.en: And in this world of business, that has helped me a lot because by the time they think that I don't know what's going on, I done got the money and gone.
sentences.zh: 在这个商业世界里，这帮了我大忙，因为当他们觉得我还搞不懂状况时，我已经把钱赚到手并抽身而去了。

sentences.en: She dressed the way she wanted to dress.
sentences.zh: 她穿自己想穿的衣服。

sentences.en: I love being flashy.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢浮夸的风格。

sentences.en: I love kind of showing the parts of me that I've become famous for and try to do it in as good a taste as I can.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢展示那些让我成名的个人特质，并尽我所能做到高雅。

sentences.en: She wasn't going to let anybody tell her what she had to look like.
sentences.zh: 她绝不会让任何人对她的外表指手画脚。

sentences.en: And, you know, even the fact that she was child-free and was not being questioned as being, you know, less than a woman,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，甚至连她选择不生育、且没有被质疑不够女人这件事，

sentences.en: that too was something that Gloria Steinem wanted for women.
sentences.zh: 这也是格洛丽亚·斯泰纳姆希望为女性争取的东西。

sentences.en: That they could make that choice and not be judged for it.
sentences.zh: 她们可以做出那样的选择而不受评判。

sentences.en: All of these things made her somebody who was living the feminist ideals in practice.
sentences.zh: 所有这些，都让她成为了一个在实践中践行女性主义理想的人。

sentences.en: Well, that makes me wonder, what, if anything, did Gloria Steinem have to say about Dolly Parton?
sentences.zh: 这让我想知道，格洛丽亚·斯泰纳姆对多莉·帕顿有过什么评价吗（如果有的话）？

sentences.en: Or I guess the other way around.
sentences.zh: 或者反过来也一样。

sentences.en: Did they see themselves as peers and in the fight together?
sentences.zh: 他们是否视彼此为志同道合的战友？

sentences.en: You know, that's a great question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常棒的问题。

sentences.en: You know, Dolly Parton went really far out of her way in interviews leading up to 9 to 5
sentences.zh: 你知道的，在《朝九晚五》上映前的采访中，多莉·帕顿特意极力撇清，

sentences.en: to say that this was absolutely not a movie about structural sexism or, you know, workplace injustice.
sentences.zh: 说这绝对不是一部关于结构性性别歧视或职场不公的电影。

sentences.en: This was not a feminist movie.
sentences.zh: 这不是一部女性主义电影。

sentences.en: It was just a funny movie about this one guy and his three wacky secretaries.
sentences.zh: 这只是一部关于一个男人和他三个古怪女秘书的搞笑电影。

sentences.en: And I think what was happening there, you know, you could look at it cynically and say, oh, this is a woman who was terrified of losing her audience in the South.
sentences.zh: 我想当时的情况是这样的，你可以用愤世嫉俗的眼光来看待它，说这是一个害怕失去南方观众支持的女性。

sentences.en: But I think that you have to interpret this decision through the lens of who we know her to be, which was this unbelievable philanthropist and visionary and champion of literacy.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，你必须透过我们所熟知的她的为人来解读这个决定——她是一位不可思议的慈善家、富有远见的思想家和扫盲倡导者。

sentences.en: And she was by then a very unifying figure, which, you know, just look at how the country has come together to grieve her loss, just as we have Gloria Steinem's loss.
sentences.zh: 到那时，她已经是一个极具凝聚力的公众人物，你看，正如整个国家聚在一起哀悼她的离去一样，就像我们哀悼格洛丽亚·斯泰纳姆的离去那样。

sentences.en: But I think she recognized that there were other people who could claim the mantle of feminism
sentences.zh: 但我认为她意识到，会有其他人来扛起女性主义的大旗

sentences.en: and do that work, but that only Dolly Parton could champion women's rights and their right
sentences.zh: 并去完成那些工作，而只有多莉·帕顿才能在不自贴标签的情况下，捍卫女性的权利以及她们在各方各面获得平等的权利，

sentences.en: to be equals in every way without labeling herself, and that she could rally people around the cause and be more effective in it if she didn't take on any kind of a label.
sentences.zh: 并且如果不给自己贴上任何标签，她就能将人们凝聚在这一事业周围，从而发挥更大的影响力。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Did Gloria Steinem ever say anything about that?
sentences.zh: 格loria Steinem对这事说过什么吗？

sentences.en: What did she think about that subtler approach?
sentences.zh: 她对那种更微妙的方法有什么看法？

sentences.en: Well, in 1987, Ms. Magazine includes Dolly Parton as one of its Women of the Year.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在1987年，《Ms.》杂志将多莉·帕顿列为年度女性之一。

sentences.en: And no one other than Gloria Steinem herself actually writes this tribute to Dolly Parton.
sentences.zh: 而且这篇向多莉·帕顿致敬的文章，竟然是由格loria Steinem本人亲自撰写的。

sentences.en: And you have to remember, back in 1987, Dolly Parton was, you know, in some circles, as much a punchline as she was an icon.
sentences.zh: 你必须记住，在1987年，多莉·帕顿在某些圈子里，与其说是一个偶像，不如说是一个笑柄。

sentences.en: And here's Gloria Steinem recognizing the work that she undoubtedly did do for the cause, whether she would own it in that language of feminism or not.
sentences.zh: 而在这里，格loria Steinem认可了她为这项事业实实在在地做出的贡献，无论她是否会用那种女性主义的语境来承认这一点。

sentences.en: What does Steinem write in this tribute to Parton?
sentences.zh: Steinem在这篇致敬帕顿的文章中写了些什么？

sentences.en: She starts like this.
sentences.zh: 她是这样开头的。

sentences.en: People who haven't listened to Dolly Parton or feminism may be surprised to learn that they go together.
sentences.zh: 没有听过多莉·帕顿或不了解女性主义的人可能会惊讶地发现，这两者是相通的。

sentences.en: And she goes on to say that if you don't understand that, you're missing something.
sentences.zh: 接着她写道，如果你不明白这一点，你就错过了一些东西。

sentences.en: Here's what she says.
sentences.zh: 她是这么说的。

sentences.en: If feminism means each of us finding our unique power and helping other women do the same,
sentences.zh: 如果女性主义意味着我们每个人找到自己独特的内在力量并帮助其他女性做同样的事，

sentences.en: Dolly Parton certainly has done both.
sentences.zh: 多莉·帕顿无疑两点都做到了。

sentences.en: So Steinem is saying, quite formally, that, yes, Dolly Parton may reject the label feminiSt.
sentences.zh: 所以Steinem很正式地在说，是的，多莉·帕顿可能会拒绝“女性主义者”这个标签。

sentences.en: And you might not think of her as a feminist, but I am here to say, as the embodiment of feminism, as its patron saint, that she is a feminist figure.
sentences.zh: 你可能不会把她当成女性主义者，但我在这里要说，作为女性主义的化身、作为它的守护圣徒，她就是一个女性主义人物。

sentences.en: And she's done the work.
sentences.zh: 而且她付出了行动。

sentences.en: And she's walked the walk.
sentences.zh: 她言行一致。

sentences.en: Like, yeah, that she's, she has that power.
sentences.zh: 就像，是的，她拥有那种力量。

sentences.en: That's the word that I think really sticks out for me.
sentences.zh: 这是我认为真正让我印象深刻的一个词。

sentences.en: This episode is about the way you've experienced these two women.
sentences.zh: 这一集讲的是你对这两位女性的体验。

sentences.en: But the way I've experienced their death is that I don't think anyone could have ever imagined that they would both die so close to each other.
sentences.zh: 但对于她们的离世，我的感受是，我想没有人会想象到她们会相继离世得如此之近。

sentences.en: And I don't think any of us really understood that either was even close to death.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为我们谁也没有真正意识到她们中任何一个人竟然离死亡那么近。

sentences.en: You know, it's funny, because when I did interview Gloria Steinem, she actually spoke a little bit about what she imagined for the end of her life.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这很有趣，因为当我采访格loria Steinem时，她确实稍微谈到了她对晚年生活的想象。

sentences.en: Here's what she said.
sentences.zh: 她是这么说的。

sentences.en: In my old age, really old age, since I'm going to live past 100, I hope, I would love to have a diner.
sentences.zh: 在我的晚年，真正的晚年，既然我希望自己能活过100岁，我很想开一家小餐馆。

sentences.en: A little diner with blue gingham curtains by the side of the road, because diners are the most democratic places.
sentences.zh: 路边一家挂着蓝色格子布窗帘的小餐馆，因为餐馆是最民主的地方。

sentences.en: And she goes on to talk about how everybody goes to diners, truck drivers, people from the neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 接着她谈到每个人都去餐馆，卡车司机，附近居民。

sentences.en: They're cheerful.
sentences.zh: 它们充满欢声笑语。

sentences.en: They're cozy.
sentences.zh: 它们温馨舒适。

sentences.en: She says they're truly populist places.
sentences.zh: 她说这里是真正的平民化场所。

sentences.en: And when I think about that diner,
sentences.zh: 每当我想起那家餐馆，

sentences.en: I can just imagine who's playing on the jukebox.
sentences.zh: 我仿佛就能想象到点唱机里正放着谁的歌。

sentences.en: It's Dolly.
sentences.zh: 是多莉。

sentences.en: Well, Sue, thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 好的，Sue，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们很感激。

sentences.en: The project has provoked opposition from preservationists and local residents because it would disrupt the views of multiple historical sites around the Capitol,

sentences.en: a single holdout appears to be preventing the jury from reaching a unanimous verdict.
